substances.name: Adrenaline (epinephrine)
doseCandidates: Adult cardiac arrest: 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 min
Anaphylaxis adult and child >12 years: 500 micrograms (0.5 mg) IM using 1 mg/mL, repeat after 5 min if no improvement
substances.clinicalNote: IM adrenaline is first-line in anaphylaxis. Antihistamines and steroids must not delay treatment of airway/breathing/circulation compromise.

substances.name: Atropine
doseCandidates: Adult symptomatic bradycardia: 1 mg IV bolus, repeat every 3–5 min, max total 3 mg
substances.clinicalNote: The user's 0.5 mg adult dose is outdated and is not stored as the current rule.

substances.name: Verapamil
doseCandidates: Adult PSVT or ventricular-rate reduction in atrial flutter/fibrillation: 5–10 mg slow IV over 2 min; if needed a further 5 mg after 5–10 min
substances.clinicalNote: Continuous ECG and BP monitoring. Avoid in marked hypotension, uncompensated heart failure, important conduction disease and accessory-pathway AF/flutter contexts.

substances.name: Propranolol
substances.clinicalNote: The raw 1–5 mg IV anxiety/hypertension note is not activated without a formulation-specific authoritative source and monitoring context.

substances.name: Amiodarone
doseCandidates: Refractory VF/pulseless VT: first 300 mg IV/IO bolus, second 150 mg IV/IO bolus
substances.clinicalNote: Non-arrest tachyarrhythmia regimens are separate monitored infusion rules and are not inherited from the cardiac-arrest rule.

substances.name: Dopamine
doseCandidates: Adult symptomatic bradycardia when atropine ineffective: 5–20 micrograms/kg/min IV infusion, titrate to response and taper slowly

substances.name: Labetalol
doseCandidates: Severe hypertension requiring rapid hospital IV control: 50 mg IV over at least 1 min; may repeat 50 mg every 5 min; total max 200 mg
substances.clinicalNote: The raw 20→40→80 mg q10min / max 300 mg scheme is not stored as the default because it does not match this selected SmPC.

substances.name: Etamsylate
substances.clinicalNote: No blanket emergency haemorrhage rule is activated. Cause-specific haemostasis and local bleeding control take priority.

substances.name: Chloropyramine
substances.clinicalNote: Brand-to-INN mapping is retained as a candidate but exact product and SmPC must be verified before a 20 mg IV/IM rule is activated. Antihistamines do not treat anaphylactic ABC compromise.

substances.name: Dexamethasone
doseCandidates: General emergency parenteral range in the selected SmPC: 3.3–16.6 mg IV/IM; exact indication must select the rule
substances.clinicalNote: Not activated as a routine first-line anaphylaxis dose; IM adrenaline remains the life-saving first-line treatment.

substances.name: Methylprednisolone
substances.clinicalNote: The product is indicated for severe allergic states including anaphylaxis, but a universal 40–125 mg rule is not activated without exact product/posology selection.

substances.name: Diclofenac
doseCandidates: Juvenile chronic arthritis age 1–12 y, suppository: 1–3 mg/kg/DAY divided into 2–3 doses
Acute post-operative pain age 6–12 y, suppository: 1–2 mg/kg/DAY in divided doses, max 4 days
substances.clinicalNote: The raw 1–2 mg/kg PER DOSE 2–3 times/day is excluded because it would materially overstate the cited paediatric SmPC dose.

substances.name: Ketoprofen
substances.clinicalNote: The label 'hypoallergenic' is explicitly rejected; NSAID hypersensitivity and bronchospasm risk remain relevant.

substances.name: Tramadol
doseCandidates: Moderate-severe pain, adults/adolescents >12 y: 50–100 mg IV/IM every 4–6 h; max 400 mg/day
substances.clinicalNote: IV doses are administered slowly. Dependence, respiratory/CNS effects and interacting serotonergic/seizure-risk medicines require review.

substances.name: Morphine
doseCandidates: Severe pain, adults/adolescents >12 y: starting IV 2.5–10 mg, inject slowly over 4–5 min and titrate to response
substances.clinicalNote: No rigid NSAID→tramadol→morphine automatic ladder is encoded.

substances.name: Paracetamol
substances.clinicalNote: Use the existing source-backed DRX paediatric rules and exact product concentration for mL conversion; do not create a duplicate generic rule.

substances.name: Ibuprofen
doseCandidates: Labelled paediatric suspension for short-term fever/pain: 20–30 mg/kg/day divided into equal doses at 6–8 h intervals
substances.clinicalNote: Actual mL requires the selected product concentration and age/weight table.

substances.name: Diazepam
substances.clinicalNote: A universal 5–10 mg IV rule is not activated for all seizure/anxiety contexts; age, indication, route and respiratory monitoring must be explicit.

substances.name: Metoclopramide
doseCandidates: Adult PONV prevention: 10 mg IV/IM single dose
Adult symptomatic nausea/vomiting or RINV: 10 mg per dose, up to 3 times/day; max 30 mg/day or 0.5 mg/kg/day; at least 6 h between doses; IV over at least 3 min
Age 1–18 y for labelled second-line indications: 0.1–0.15 mg/kg IV up to 3 times/day; max 0.5 mg/kg/day
substances.clinicalNote: Extrapyramidal reactions are possible. DRX does not encode an automatic fixed 'Akiniton antidote' instruction.

substances.name: Biperiden
substances.clinicalNote: Active-substance candidate for Akiniton; an acute dystonia rescue rule requires exact product evidence before activation.

substances.name: Hyoscine butylbromide
doseCandidates: Adults with acute spasm/renal or biliary colic: 20 mg IV/IM; may repeat after 30 min; max 100 mg/day
substances.clinicalNote: Severe unexplained abdominal pain requires diagnostic investigation; this injection SmPC does not recommend paediatric use.

substances.name: Ondansetron
doseCandidates: Adult PONV prevention/treatment: 4 mg IM or slow IV single dose
Paediatric PONV: 0.1 mg/kg slow IV, max 4 mg
substances.clinicalNote: Do not generalise these PONV rules to gastroenteritis or CINV without the appropriate indication branch.

substances.name: Furosemide
doseCandidates: Adults when prompt parenteral diuresis is required: initial 20–50 mg IV/IM; larger doses are titrated/infused according to response
substances.clinicalNote: Potassium is not automatically prescribed after furosemide; monitor electrolytes and replace when clinically indicated.

substances.name: Sodium bicarbonate
substances.clinicalNote: No blanket 50 mmol arrest/acidosis rule. Dose is acid-base- and indication-specific; routine undifferentiated cardiac-arrest administration is excluded.

substances.name: Sodium chloride 0.9% IV solution
substances.clinicalNote: Bolus volume depends on indication, age, cardiac/renal status and response. DRX does not publish a universal 500–1000 mL bolus for every hypotension/shock presentation.

substances.name: Glucose 5% IV solution
substances.clinicalNote: Not a resuscitation crystalloid and not encoded as a diuretic treatment for hypertension.

substances.name: Glucose 50% IV solution
substances.clinicalNote: Concentrated dextrose rescue dosing and venous-access precautions are formulation/protocol specific.

substances.name: Ringer's lactate / Hartmann's solution
substances.clinicalNote: Balanced crystalloid use is volume-status-, electrolyte- and indication-dependent; no universal fixed bolus is activated.

substances.name: Mannitol
doseCandidates: Adults/adolescents for reduction of intracranial pressure/cerebral volume or elevated intraocular pressure: 1.5–2 g/kg IV over 30–60 min
substances.clinicalNote: The raw 0.25–1 g/kg value is not used as this source's default; renal function, osmolality and blood-brain-barrier context require monitoring.
